name: dialog
description: A modal window over a dimmed page that takes focus until it closes: confirmations, short forms, details. Put a trigger button and a Dialog inside DialogTrigger, then compose DialogTitle, DialogDescription and DialogFooter (actions, right-aligned) inside the Dialog, all exported from the dialog file. A button with slot="close" closes it; Escape always does. Add DialogClose, an X in the top-right corner, to dialogs that inform or collect input; pass aria-label to translate its "Close" name. Use role="alertdialog" for a decision such as a delete confirmation, and leave DialogClose out of it: Cancel is the way out. To open it from code or a menu item, skip DialogTrigger and control isOpen. The example's Button comes from the button component.

props.name: children
props.description: DialogTitle, then the content, then DialogFooter. A function receives close.

props.name: role
props.description: alertdialog for a decision the user must make; screen readers then also read DialogDescription.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Close on a click outside. Leave off for dialogs that ask for a decision.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state, for a dialog opened without a DialogTrigger; pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog asks to open or close: Escape, a close button, a click outside.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names a dialog that has no DialogTitle.

example:
<DialogTrigger>
  <Button variant="danger">Delete project</Button>
  <Dialog role="alertdialog">
    <DialogTitle>Delete project?</DialogTitle>
    <DialogDescription>This removes every file in it.</DialogDescription>
    <DialogFooter>
      <Button slot="close" variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="danger" onPress={remove}>Delete</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </Dialog>
</DialogTrigger>
